title: Hedged prefetch and light SDK proposal for hosted streaming
content:
Summary:
This doc proposes a lightweight SDK surface and a hedged-prefetch policy for the Hosted API to improve p50/p90 interactive latency for tool-heavy flows while keeping host costs predictable and preserving structured output guarantees. The idea: let clients express a small speculative prefetch plan (1–3 hedged tool/variant requests) with cost and latency caps. The server schedules hedged attempts across priority lanes, returns progressive structured frames, and exposes observability and cost tokens to clients so they can surface fallbacks deterministically.

Background & problem:
- Increasing number of integrations require the model to call external tools (search, code-run, DB lookups) during a single streaming response.
- Naive synchronous tool calls blow up end-to-end latency and make client UX janky.
- Clients often overfetch or issue many retries; platform sees unpredictable token and RPC costs.
- Current hosted streaming surfaces support partial output, but do not provide a principled way for speculative hedging while preserving cost visibility and structured output semantics.

Goals:
- Reduce median latency for tool-augmented streams by enabling speculative tool prefetch/hedging.
- Keep per-request cost caps explicit and enforceable by both client and server.
- Surface progressive structured outputs so clients can deterministically fallback when hedged attempts fail or are truncated.
- Maintain simple SDK ergonomics: single-stream object, non-blocking callbacks, low memory on thin clients (mobile/web).

Non-goals:
- This is not a full orchestration runtime for long-running tool pipelines.
- We are not changing billing model here — hedging counts toward usage; we provide visibility and caps.

Key concepts and vocabulary:
- Prefetch Plan: a short list (N<=3) of speculative tool invocations or model variant calls the client asks the server to attempt in parallel/sequence. Each entry includes an optimistic cost budget and a latency budget.
- Hedged lane: internal scheduling lane that runs speculative calls with lower resource priority (can be preempted).
- Commit frame: the structured output frame that marks the selected/committed tool results for downstream consumption.
- Lease token: short-lived token clients receive for speculative responses; used to reconcile and replay if a commit is later confirmed.
- Cost passport: a summarized accounting token returned periodically for the stream that shows cumulative counted tokens and RPCs against the request caps.

Surface and protocol (sketch):
- Client opens a streaming session: POST /v1/stream/sessions -> returns session_id, ws_url or streaming URL.
- When sending a prompt, client can include an optional prefetched_plan field in the initiation frame: e.g. { "prefetch_plan": [{"tool":"search","budget_usd":0.003,"latency_ms":120},{"tool":"code_eval","budget_usd":0.02,"latency_ms":500}] }
- Server acknowledges with accepted_plan (may shrink or reject entries).
- Server sends progressive frames: partial_text, partial_structured_frames, speculative_tool_frames (tagged as speculative + lease_token).
- When a speculative attempt completes and is chosen, server emits a commit_frame referencing the speculative lease_token and a small diff that upgrades the speculative_frame -> committed_frame. If speculative attempts do not finish within budgets, server emits a deterministic fallback commit (e.g., "no-tool" or best-effort summary).

Example minimal client flow (pseudo):
1) open session -> session_123
2) send prompt with prefetch_plan [search(120ms), external-kb(250ms)]
3) receive frames:
   - partial_text: "Here's a plan..."
   - speculative_tool_frame(lease=lt_1): search results (truncated)
   - partial_structured: {"steps":[{"desc":"…","source":"speculative:lt_1"}]}
4) later receive commit: commit(lease=lt_1, final_tool_result) and passport update shows budget used.

SDK ergonomics (recommendations):
- Single lightweight Stream object per session with: onText(chunk), onStructured(frame), onSpeculative(lease,frame), onCommit(lease,frame), onPassport(update), onError(err).
- Backpressure API: stream.requestMore(n) to inform server of client appetite for more speculative lanes. For low-end clients, default to 0 speculative lanes unless explicitly opted-in.
- Small binary-friendly framing for mobile: prefer delta JSONL frames with a small header for frame type and lease token.
- Convenience helper: SDK exposes a PrefetchPlan builder that validates budgets and translates client-side simple hints ("fast-search", "low-cost-eval") into the platform’s plan structures.

Observability and billing visibility:
- Cost passport frames emitted every ~500ms or on significant events. Passport includes tokens_considered, estimate_usd, rpc_count, and plan_attachments.
- Trace correlation IDs: hedged attempts, lease tokens, and commit frames must include trace ids so we can reconstruct end-to-end timeline in Console.
- Telemetry knobs: platform exposes a tenant-level hedging rate limit and per-account hedged concurrency cap.

Operational policies & safety:
- By default, speculative frames are annotated ephemeral and are not stored long-term unless explicitly persisted by the client during commit.
- Speculative outputs are rate-limited and accounted; accidental overuse is prevented by the platform rejecting plans that exceed configured account caps.
- There will be model-level safety filters applied before speculative tool frames are surfaced to client if the tool returns untrusted content.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP):
- Platform accepts and executes a prefetch_plan for streaming requests with N<=3 and returns speculative frames and commit frames as described.
- SDKs (JS + Python) implement the Stream object API and PrefetchPlan builder with unit tests and examples.
- Console shows hedged attempt traces and cost passport in request timeline.
- E2E perf: for benchmark scenario (a 2-tool composition), p50 latency improves by >=25% with hedging enabled and within a 1.5x cost overhead for typical budgets.

Migration and backward compatibility:
- Clients that do not include prefetch_plan will continue to operate as today.
- Server will fall back to non-speculative execution for older clients.
- SDK helper will include a migration guide: "how to add hedged prefetch safely".

Risks and open questions:
- Cost inflation: clients may misuse hedging and cause large bill variance. Mitigation: conservative defaults, quotas, and clear passport visibility.
- Complexity in ordering partial frames and commits across network interruptions. Need robust resume semantics (session snapshots) and well-defined idempotency for commit frames.
- UX ambiguity: when to show speculative content vs commit content to end users. SDK should provide clear flags and helpers for UI adoption.

Next steps (short-term roadmap):
- Spike (2 weeks): implement server-side scheduler prototype for hedged lanes + minimal passport emission.
- SDK sprint (1 week): JS and Py builders + demo app (search+summarize) that exercises hedging.
- Benchmarks (1 week): run p50/p90 perf + cost tradeoff matrices across a small set of customer workloads.
- Review & iterate: share with Solutions Eng and SRE for load modeling; incorporate safety filter plan.

Open design items to resolve before alpha:
- Exact passport schema (fields and emission cadence).
- Lease token TTL semantics and replay API for commit reconciliation.
- Backpressure heuristics and default speculative lanes per client type.
- UI conventions for speculative content in Console and SDK examples.

Appendix: short checklist for implementation
- [ ] API: session open, send prompt with prefetch plan, ack accepted_plan
- [ ] Server: hedged lane scheduler, speculative frame tagging, commit diff emission
- [ ] SDK: Stream object, PrefetchPlan helper, requestMore backpressure method
- [ ] Telemetry: passport frames, trace ids across leases, Console visualization
